screens.layout_summary: The hub is five baked panes on a full-screen cloth: a vertical COMMAND LIST window (Item/Ability/Equip/Status/Order/Card/Config — 7 rows, one column) bound at SubMenuPanel.GetChild(0).GetChild(0) (MainMenuUI.cs:694-700); a column of 4 CHARACTER PLATES (portrait + name/Lv + HP + MP + magic stones + status icons) bound by iterating CharacterListPanel.transform (783-797); a GIL+PLAYTIME window (GenericInfoPanel — child 0 = time hh:mm:ss with 2 colon labels, child 1 = gil, 799-807); a LOCATION-NAME window (LocationInfoPanel, name label = child 0, 808) whose left edge is runtime-anchored 30px from the screen's left edge (815-817), so it hugs the screen border even in widescreen; and a PC-only help/description label (HelpDespLabelGameObject, shown only when FF9StateSystem.PCPlatform, 57). Behind everything sits GOMenuBackground: the baked "menu_bg" sprite is re-pointed to "main_menu_bg" and stretched to the full UIContentSize (1543x1080 pillarboxed, or 1080*aspect wide in widescreen) with a "background_gradient" shadow child (MainMenuUI.cs:819; GOMenuBackground.cs:19-33; UIManager.cs:653-666). Pane positions themselves are BAKED (only GetChild bindings visible); the code-visible geometry is: command rows are 402 wide with pivot x=201 inside their table (721), the vanilla row pitch is 98 UI units with a 9-unit top inset (implied by every ShiftContentClip = (0, 9 + rowIndex*98): 154/247/258/269/184/196), and character-plate avatars sit at local x=-418 (front row) / -392 (back row) (15-16). Visually the screen reads exactly like PSX FF9's hub: plates left-of-center, command column right, info windows in the corners. Sub-screens are SEPARATE UIScenes; the hub hands off by collapsing its command window down to the chosen row (HonoTweenClipping) while the target scene fades in, and every sub-screen's Hide path calls MainMenuScene.StartSubmenuTweenIn() to regrow the command window on the way back (AbilityUI.cs:286, ItemUI.cs:215, CardUI.cs:42, ConfigUI.cs:658, EquipUI.cs:114, StatusUI.cs:88, PartySettingUI.cs:161).

panes.name: SubMenuPanel (command-list window)
panes.geometry: Baked position; rows inside its child(0).child(0) UITable are 402 wide, pivot x=201; when Memoria inserts the optional Party row it re-lays ALL rows imperatively: SetRawRect(201, y, 402, h) with y starting -39, h alternating 79/78, gap 8, BoxCollider sized to match, UITable then DISABLED (MainMenuUI.cs:717-726). Vanilla baked pitch = 98/row + 9 top inset (from ShiftContentClip math, 154/247/258/269/184/196)
panes.notes: 7 baked rows = children 0-6 in enum order Item..Config (694-700). Disabled rows are painted FF9TextTool.Gray, enabled White (64-72). Window-color swept explicitly at Show (50). Tagged sprites re-atlased, not per-row.

panes.name: CharacterListPanel (4 party plates)
panes.geometry: Baked; 4 child cells iterated at Awake (783-797). Avatar local x=-418 front row / -392 back row, y=0 (FrontRowPosition/BackRowPosition, 15-16) — a 26px x-shift encodes battle row
panes.notes: Each plate doubles as a button in group MainMenu.Character; its child(1) is the separate Order-target button (791-794). Plates are the tween-in subjects (TweenIn [0,1,2,3], 59). Dead character = avatar alpha 0.5 (FF9UIDataTool.cs:172). Empty slot = Content SetActive(false) (505).

panes.notes: Playtime label color cycles every 100h (360000s): White/Red/Yellow/Cyan/Magenta/Green, capped 99:59:59 green (521-560). Updated every frame in Update (681-685). Gil via 'GilSymbol' localization replace (512).

panes.name: LocationInfoPanel (location-name window)

panes.notes: PC-only static description label. The REAL help grammar is per-button: ButtonGroupState.Help.TextKey / .Text on each row and plate, incl. rich text with [ICON=625+i], [SPRT=item##_##,64,64], [FEED], [XTAB=82|64] markup for Equip/Status target help (432-486).

panes.name: Background (scene root child 4)

panes.notes: HonoFading component = UIScene.FadingComponent (693). Show also pre-sets the event fade black: SceneDirector.FadeEventSetColor(FadeMode.Sub, Color.black) (46).

panes.name: TransitionGroup / SubMenuTransitionGameObject
panes.geometry: TransitionGroup.child(0) carries HonoTweenPosition (characterTransition, 809); SubMenuTransitionGameObject carries HonoTweenClipping (submenuTransition, 810)
panes.notes: Pure animation rigs, no visible chrome of their own; the clipping rig owns a serialized ClipPanel + ScaleGameObject + BGSprite + ShiftContentGameObject (HonoTweenClipping.cs:198-202).

lists.name: Command list (SubMenu rows)
lists.grammar: 1 column x 7 visible rows (no scrolling, no scrollbar, no caption header) — baked children 0-6 of SubMenuPanel.child(0).child(0), a UITable (MainMenuUI.cs:694-700,703). Cell = one GameObject carrying UIWidget + BoxCollider + UIButton + UIKeyNavigation + ButtonGroupState(with Help) + UIEventListener.Click (704-706,712-715,721-722,771-777), with child(0) = the label GO holding UILocalize + UILabel (705, 64-70). colW=402, cell pivot x=201; runtime relaid rowH alternates 79/78 with an 8 gap (pitch 87/86) when the optional Party row is inserted and the UITable is disabled (717-726); VANILLA baked pitch = 98 with 9 top inset, proven by the transition shift constants 9+98*rowIndex (154,247,258,269,184,196) and the shiftFactor 7f/(7f+extraRows) that rescales them when rows are added (143). Disabled state = label Gray (64-72) + SFX 102 buzzer on confirm (230). Group name 'MainMenu.SubMenu' (838).

lists.name: Character plate list
lists.grammar: 1 column x 4 visible cells, no scrollbar — enumerated from CharacterListPanel.transform at Awake (783-797). Cell anatomy (CharacterDetailHUD.cs:10-72): Self -> child(0)=Content {child0 AvatarSprite(UISprite), child1 name group {child0 NameLabel, child2 LvLabel}, child2 HPPanel {child1 HP, child2 slash, child3 HPmax}, child3 MPPanel {same shape}, child4 MagicStone panel {child1 cur, child2 slash, child3 max} or literal 'Empty' node, child5 StatusesPanel {child0 -> 7 UISprite status icons} or 'Empty'}; Self child(1) = the Order sub-button target (791-794). Value labels use Overflow.ResizeFreely, max labels fixedAlignment (CharacterDetailHUD.cs:51-53,75-81). Avatar x=-418 front/-392 back (MainMenuUI.cs:15-16); HP/MP text color = White/Yellow(<=1/6 max)/Red(0 HP) (FF9UIDataTool.cs:119-123). Two groups share the cells: 'MainMenu.Character' (whole plate) and 'MainMenu.Order' (child-1 buttons) (839-840); nav ring is rebuilt circular over ENABLED plates only via UIKeyNavigation.onUp/onDown (667-678).

screens.depth_stack: Baked panel depths are not visible in code (GetChild bindings only). Runtime-written depths, back-to-front: the fade sheet's parent UIPanel is set by MainMenuUI.Hide — depth 7 when descending to a sub-screen (so the command-window collapse animation plays ABOVE the fade), depth 10 when exiting to gameplay (fade covers everything) (MainMenuUI.cs:94-99). Pointer (finger cursor) depths are per button-group: 10 for MainMenu.SubMenu, 12 for MainMenu.Order (417-418, via ButtonGroupState.SetPointerDepthToGroup which stashes into pointerDepthList, ButtonGroupState.cs:220-223); the Order pointer must beat the plate pointer since both cursors can coexist (secondary-group hold, 171-172/281). Note these are PANEL depths in NGUI's separate-UIPanel sort model.
screens.pointer: 3 button groups: 'MainMenu.SubMenu', 'MainMenu.Character', 'MainMenu.Order' (MainMenuUI.cs:838-840). Pointer config set once in AfterShowCharacter (413-430): depth 10 SubMenu group, depth 12 Order group (417-418); finger offsets LTR = (10,0) Character, (30,-28) Order; RTL = (80,0) Character, (100,-28) Order (419-427). NO pointer limit rect is set for any hub group (SetPointerLimitRectToGroup never called here — that idiom belongs to scrolling lists). Cursor memory: SetCursorStartSelect(currentMenu row) + RemoveCursorMemorize on SubMenu at every show (415-416, 24-25); characterMemorize / characterOrderMemorize GameObjects persist the plate cursor per mode (167-169,177, 245/256/267/278, 341-343), wiped only on full exit (117-126). Group state machine: entering Ability/Equip/Status/Order flips ActiveGroup to Character with SetSecondaryOnGroup + HoldActiveStateOnGroup on SubMenu (170-172,178-180); Order goes one deeper (279-281). Mouse shortcut: clicking a row while deep in Character/Order simulates muted cancels then a confirm (OnSecondaryGroupClick, 392-411).
screens.transitions: ENTER: base.Show fades via HonoFading with fadeOutDuration = Configuration.Interface.FadeDuration (/FastForwardFactor when fast-forwarding) (UIScene.cs:52-56); MainMenuUI.Show pre-sets event fade black (FadeEventSetColor(Sub, black), 46), sweeps window color, then if arriving from gameplay (isNeedCharacterTween) slides all 4 character plates in: characterTransition.TweenIn([0,1,2,3]) (59) — HonoTweenPosition defaults: from x=1543 (offscreen right), duration 0.4s, per-plate delayList stagger, resetAnchorDelay 0.2 (HonoTweenPosition.cs:280-290). EXIT to gameplay (Cancel on SubMenu group): SFX 101, NeedTweenAndHideSubMenu=true, fade panel depth 10, cursor memories cleared, FF9Wipe_FadeInEx(12) + SubMenuPanel.SetActive(false) in the after-hide (79-104,318-336). EXIT to a sub-screen (Confirm): SFX 103; the command window COLLAPSES to the chosen row — submenuTransition.TweenOut with AnimationTime = Configuration.Interface.FadeDuration (100-101,108) and ShiftContentClip = (0, 9 + shiftFactor*98*rowIndex) so the shrinking clip stays centered on the selected row (154,247,258,269,184,196; shiftFactor=7/(7+optional rows), 143); fade panel depth 7 keeps the collapse visible (99); the selected row's UIButton is reset to Normal state (155 etc.); then ChangeUIState to the target scene inside the hide callback. RETURN: every sub-screen's back-out calls MainMenuScene.StartSubmenuTweenIn() (106-110; AbilityUI.cs:286, ItemUI.cs:215, CardUI.cs:42, ConfigUI.cs:658+789-790, EquipUI.cs:114, StatusUI.cs:88, PartySettingUI.cs:161) which regrows the window (HonoTweenClipping.TweenIn restores defaultClipScale/defaultSpriteScale captured at its Awake, HonoTweenClipping.cs:7-16,60-81). SFX ids: 103 confirm (148,237,302), 101 cancel (324,339,348), 102 denied/buzzer (230). Order changes never leave the scene (toggle row or swap members in place, 622-639).
screens.window_color: Scene-wide sweep, not per-row: base.Show calls DisplayWindowBackground() on the scene root — every UISprite tagged 'Window Color' (whose atlas is not General/Icon) is re-atlased to FF9UIDataTool.WindowAtlas (UIScene.cs:48, 261-273). MainMenuUI.Show additionally sweeps the SubMenuPanel subtree explicitly: this.DisplayWindowBackground(this.SubMenuPanel, null) (MainMenuUI.cs:50) — needed because the command window can be inactive during the sweep on some paths (SubMenuPanel.SetActive toggles at 56/87/114).
screens.widescreen_pass: MainMenuUI has NO UpdateUserInterface — the hub is never re-dimensioned by Memoria's widescreen relayout (grep across the tree finds UpdateUserInterface only on sub-screens: Ability/Item/Status/Shop/Equip/Chocograph/Card/BattleHUD; MenuUIControlPanel.onHide re-runs the SUB-screens' passes, MenuUIControlPanel.cs:52-56). The hub's aspect adaptation is three Awake writes plus the background: (1) LocationInfoPanel's UIWidget leftAnchor retargeted to the scene root, Set(0f, 30f) — location window pinned 30px from the true screen left at any aspect (MainMenuUI.cs:815-817); (2) two info labels' rightAnchor.absolute = -40 (821-822); (3) GOMenuBackground stretches 'main_menu_bg' + 'background_gradient' to UIContentSize = 1543x1080 pillarboxed or (1080*Screen.width/Screen.height)x1080 in widescreen (GOMenuBackground.cs:22-23,31-32; UIManager.cs:653-666). The one true runtime RE-LAYOUT in this file is aspect-independent: Memoria's optional Party-row insert clones the Card row and hand-lays all 8 rows — SetRawRect(201, y, 402, h), y from -39, h alternating 79/78, gap 8, colliders resized, UITable disabled (701-727) — compressing the baked 98-pitch to 87/86-pitch to fit the extra row in the same window.
idioms: GetChild-chain scene binding in Awake IS the baked-hierarchy record: e.g. rows = SubMenuPanel.GetChild(0).GetChild(0).GetChild(0..6) (MainMenuUI.cs:694-700); labels = GenericInfoPanel.GetChild(0).GetChild(1..5) (799-807)

Runtime row-clone idiom (Memoria's Party row = the precedent our Folklore row copied): Instantiate an existing row, swap its UILocalize key + Help.TextKey, reparent so Config stays last, rewire the UIKeyNavigation onUp/onDown ring, hand-lay every row with SetRawRect + matching BoxCollider, then DISABLE the UITable — there is no auto-reflow (701-727)
Named static button groups + an ActiveGroup state machine replaces any 'screen stack': OnKeyConfirm/OnKeyCancel branch purely on ButtonGroupState.ActiveGroup (144,233,298,322,337,346)
Two-level drill-in keeps the shallower group visibly selected: SetSecondaryOnGroup + HoldActiveStateOnGroup (171-172,178-180,281)
Per-group cursor memory GameObjects (characterMemorize/characterOrderMemorize) + SetCursorMemorize/SetCursorStartSelect/RemoveCursorMemorize (24-25,167-169,177,415-416,452-468 in ButtonGroupState.cs)
Help text lives ON the button: ButtonGroupState.Help.TextKey for static keys, .Text for composed rich text with [ICON]/[SPRT=name,64,64]/[FEED]/[XTAB] markup (432-486)
Disabled-row grammar: label color White vs Gray at Show + buzzer SFX 102 on confirm attempt, row object stays clickable (64-72,228-231)

The submenu handoff pair: HonoTweenClipping.TweenOut on leave with ShiftContentClip aimed at the selected row, and the TARGET scene's Hide path calling StartSubmenuTweenIn to regrow — the collapse/regrow is owned by the HUB, invoked by the sub-screens (106-110; AbilityUI.cs:286 et al.)
Fade-panel depth is a per-path runtime write, not baked: 7 to keep an animation visible during descent, 10 to cover everything on exit (94-99)
DisplayWindowBackground sweep = tag-driven re-atlas of 'Window Color' sprites; call it on any subtree that might have been inactive during the scene-root sweep (50; UIScene.cs:266-273)
Avatar row shift: battle row is encoded as a 26px avatar x-offset (-418 front / -392 back) applied by FF9UIDataTool.DisplayCharacterAvatar (15-16; FF9UIDataTool.cs:173-179)

Layout constants encode the baked geometry implicitly: ShiftContentClip = (0, 9 + shiftFactor*98*rowIndex) reveals the baked 98 row pitch + 9 inset without any scene file (143,154,184,196,247,258,269)
numbers: Command row rect when hand-laid: SetRawRect(x=201, y, w=402, h) — y starts -39, h alternates 79/78, gap 8 (pitch 87/86); BoxCollider = (402, h) — MainMenuUI.cs:717-725

screens.screen: Status (StatusUI, UIState.Status) — the dense single-character sheet
screens.layout_summary: One character's full sheet on a single static screen — the only stock menu with NO cursor and NO scrolling list. The screen is a patchwork of seven fixed sub-windows over a full-screen "status_bg" cloth: a character identity pane (avatar + name/Lv + HP/MP + magic stones + status icons, with an avatar cross-fade slider for character switching), a 10-row attribute grid (Speed/Strength/Magic/Spirit | Attack/Defence/Evade/MagicDef/MagicEva, split by a baked spacer row at index 4), an ETC pane (Trance gauge + EXP + Next Lv), a 5-slot equipment pane (Weapon/Head/Wrist/Body/Accessory, each = part icon + item icon + name), and a 4-entry command bar (Attack/Ability1/Ability2/Item names, center-aligned). On top of these sits the screen's one interactive flourish: up to 6 ability sub-panels of 8 rows each that CASCADE in one per Confirm press (slide-in from the right screen edge), stacking like dealt cards, each carrying its own caption header of which only the topmost stays visible; Cancel (or a 7th Confirm) sweeps the whole cascade out. Character switching is L/R bumpers (arrow panel shown only when party>1). All pane positions/sizes are baked in the scene prefab; the code re-dimensions only a handful of labels at Awake. Which character the sheet shows is chosen BEFORE entry, on the MainMenu's character list (MainMenuUI.cs:164-173, 273) — StatusUI itself owns zero button groups.

panes.name: Background cloth (transform child 10)

panes.notes: GOMenuBackground swaps baked 'menu_bg' -> 'status_bg' when the atlas has it, and the child-0 'dialog_hilight' shadow -> full-screen 'background_gradient', both resized to UIContentSize (GOMenuBackground.cs:19-33). Accessed positionally: transform.GetChild(10) (StatusUI.cs:456) — the ONLY positional root-child access; everything else is an inspector-serialized GameObject reference (StatusUI.cs:22-32).

panes.geometry: Baked. Runtime writes: MagicStoneLabel de-anchored and forced 60x52 (StatusUI.cs:418-420)
panes.notes: Bound via CharacterDetailHUD(go,false): Content=child0; child0=AvatarSprite, child1={0:name,2:Lv}, child2=HPPanel{1:cur,2:slash,3:max}, child3=MPPanel same, child4=MagicStones{1:cur,2:slash,3:max}, child5=StatusesPanel with 7 status icon sprites (CharacterDetailHUD.cs:11-72). panes.geometry: Baked; no runtime geometry writes

lists.name: Ability cascade (the screen's only list-like structure — paged, not scrolled)
lists.grammar: 6 panels (hard-coded cap: '_currentAbilityPanelAmount < 6' / '== 6', StatusUI.cs:117,132) x 8 visible rows each (childIndex loop 0..7, StatusUI.cs:411) = 48 slots, one per pa[] ability index. NO scrollbar, NO cursor: paging is Confirm-to-deal-next-panel. Cell anatomy (AbilityItemHUD.cs:10-15): child0 = stone icon UISprite ('ability_stone' for actives, 'skill_stone_on'/'skill_stone_off' for supports — StatusUI.cs:367,374), child1 = name UILabel (fixedAlignment), child2 = APBarHUD. APBar anatomy (APBarHUD.cs:11-18): root UISprite+UISlider, child0 = foreground sprite ('ap_bar_progress' or 'ap_bar_complete'), child1 = TextPanel {0:curAP, 2:maxAP labels}, child2 = master star sprite ('ap_bar_complete_star'); mastered bars hide the TextPanel, in-progress bars show it only for isShowText abilities (FF9UIDataTool.cs:239-261). Empty/unowned slots SetActive(false) (StatusUI.cs:344-355). Caption header: per-panel baked object at GetChild(1).GetChild(3) (StatusUI.cs:413), only the topmost visible panel's caption shown (119-127). Cell dimensions baked, no runtime writes.

lists.name: Parameter grid (static 2-col x 9-row attribute table)

screens.layout_summary: The screen is a two-stage picker that swaps panes IN PLACE rather than side by side: a full-screen background cloth ("save_load_bg", scene-root child 8, Memoria-stretched to the whole UI content area), a title label ("Save"/"Load", SerailizeTitleLabel via setSerializeType, SaveLoadUI.cs:683-689), a help strip at top (HelpPanel with a slot-number label at HelpPanel/1/0, SaveLoadUI.cs:694; PC-only description label toggled at :295), and then EITHER the SlotListPanel (10 slim slot rows, "Slot 1..10") OR the FileListPanel (15 fat file rows in a snap-scrolling panel with an up/down scroll-arrow rail at FileListPanel child 0 and a header/caption pane at child 2). Slot->file and file->slot swaps are a FadePingPong crossfade of the whole scene (SaveLoadUI.cs:568-578, 242-251), so the screen always reads as ONE centered sheet over the cloth. Each fat row is itself a bordered window (its sprites are "Window Color"-tagged and re-atlased per row) carrying: a FileNo strip pinned to the row's top edge, leader name + level, gil, colored playtime clock, location name, and up to 4 party portrait sprites; empty/corrupt rows collapse to a single centered text label ("Empty"/"Corrupt", red for corrupt). Modal overlays stack on top: a loading-preview toast, a progress-bar access panel (with UISlider), a "Save successful" toast repositioned next to the saved row, an overwrite Yes/No dialog, and DialogManager speech-window notices for no-save/corrupt states. There is no left/right split and no sub-window navigation — depth comes from overlays, not from panes.

screens.layout_summary: The Equip screen is a multi-pane sheet over a full-screen 'equip_bg' cloth (root child 6, EquipUI.cs:1312). It composes: a 3-command submenu bar (Equip / Optimize / Off, EquipUI.cs:1332-1334); a character-identity window (avatar + name/Lv + HP/MP, CharacterDetailPanel via CharacterDetailHUD, EquipUI.cs:1278); a 9-row stat-COMPARE window (CharacterParameterPanel, current value | blink-arrow | preview value per row, EquipUI.cs:1279, 1394-1402); a 5-row static GEAR-PART list (Weapon/Head/Wrist/Body/Accessory, EquipmentPartListPanel child 0, EquipUI.cs:1280); an item DETAIL window (selected item header + up to 3 ability rows with AP bars, EquipmentAbilityPanel, EquipUI.cs:1283-1286); and the star of the grammar — a 752px-wide scrollable INVENTORY sub-list sheet (EquipmentInventoryListPanel wrapped as GOScrollablePanel, EquipUI.cs:1294) that is OFFSTAGE until the player confirms a gear part, then slides in via HonoTweenPosition and takes input focus. All pane positions are baked in the scene (only accessor paths visible in code); the one runtime screen-space anchor is the inventory group's pointer limit rect (-7,-49,745,325) = left/bottom/right/top (EquipUI.cs:61), placing the inventory sheet from screen-center-x to x=745, y=-49..325 — i.e. the right half, upper-middle band, in the 1080-tall center-origin space. The two lists share the screen by MODALITY, not real estate juggling: the part list is always present; the inventory sheet tweens in over the same region, the part caption hides, and ButtonGroupState.ActiveGroup decides which list owns the cursor; the part row stays visibly held (secondary group) underneath.

screens.layout_summary: Full-screen menu sheet over a dedicated background cloth ("item_bg" + a full-screen "background_gradient" shadow, both sized to UIContentSize = 1543x1080 pillarboxed or 1080*aspect widescreen). Top rail = three sub-menu buttons (Use / Arrange / Key Items) owned by this scene (the MainMenu's own SubMenuPanel is switched OFF on entry, ItemUI.cs:98, and tween-restored on exit, :215). The body is ONE list slot that two panels share by SetActive swap (ItemUI.cs:120-121, 586-599): the regular-item list (baked 2 columns x 8 visible rows of 745x98 cells: icon + name + count, with a caption header row repeating "Name/Info" per column) and the key-item list (same 1490-wide sheet, hard-locked 2 columns, name-only cells with a "New!" badge). Each list is a GOScrollablePanel: scroll-arrow assembly + clipped scroll sub-panel + caption/border background. Picking a usable item slides the use-target pane in from the opposite pillarbox edge (from x=+/-1543) to rest at x=+338 (item in left column) or x=-398 (right column): a vertical stack of 4 character rows (portrait, name, HP/MP or status list). Confirming a key item slides in a detail sheet (name label + long description label). Arrange opens a small clip-reveal dialog (Auto/Manual) framed by a GOFrameBackground. A PC-only help hint label sits on screen (ItemUI.cs:123). Reading order: cloth at the very back, list sheet center-left dominant, target pane overlapping from a side, pointer + help bubble floating on top.

screens.layout_summary: Full-screen menu over a dedicated "shop_bg" cloth (the generic "menu_bg" sprite is re-skinned to shop_bg and stretched to UIContentSize at Awake — GOMenuBackground.cs:19-23, ShopUI.cs:1299). The screen is a mode machine: a top title+help strip (ShopTitleLabel/HelpLabel, localized per mode — ShopUI.cs:684-712), a Buy/Sell submenu bar (BuySubMenu/SellSubMenu, ShopUI.cs:1443-1444), and exactly ONE of three main sheets active at a time (SetShopType deactivates all then enables one — ShopUI.cs:1202-1241): (1) ItemShopPanel = a 916-wide 1-column x 8-row buy list plus an info rail (Funds/Count; the Equipped row is force-hidden — ShopUI.cs:1259-1260); (2) WeaponAndSynthShopPanel = the same 916-wide buy list but only 5 visible rows (ShopUI.cs:78) to leave room below for the character compare pane (CharacterParamInfoPanel: a row of avatar cells each showing equip-part icon, new stat value, and an up/down change arrow, with LT/RT paging when the party exceeds the baked HUD count — ShopUI.cs:962-1043, 660-682) plus the Funds/Count/Equipped info rail; synthesis additionally lights SynthesisPartInfoPanel and a required-ingredients label anchored into the info pane (ShopUI.cs:1311-1314); (3) SellShopPanel = a wide 1490px 2-column x 8-row inventory grid (sell has no compare pane, so the list takes nearly the whole width — ShopUI.cs:157, 134). Buying/selling pops the InputQuantityDialog sub-window (icon+name+quantity spinner+total price) at localPosition (0,-16) for buy or (0,50) for sell, with the InfoDialog (Funds/Count/Equipped recap) additionally shown beneath in sell mode (ShopUI.cs:1045-1093); its host panel is raised one depth above the baked stack (ShopUI.cs:1315). Bottom edge carries one of two baked button-legend bars (NonSynthesisControlPanel/SynthesisControlPanel — ShopUI.cs:53-62). All pane positions are baked in the scene (read via GetChild paths, not runtime writes); only the list grids are re-dimensioned at runtime.

screens.layout_summary: A full-screen collection screen reached only from the field-script Menu command (menuId 5 → EventService.OpenChocoGraph, EventService.cs:23-25, 59-70), not from the main menu. It composes as: (1) a full-screen background cloth (root child 7) — stock "menu_bg" sprite + "dialog_hilight" shadow gradient, with a Memoria hook that swaps to a dedicated "chocograph_bg" only if a modded atlas supplies it (ChocographUI.cs:418, GOMenuBackground.cs:19-33); (2) ONE scrolling list sheet (ChocographListPanel) 658 units wide showing 5 rows of 86px in the stock bake (ChocographUI.cs:53-55), re-dimensioned by Memoria to 7 rows of 61px by default — 24 fixed rows total, each row = box-icon + name label, undiscovered rows rendered as blank slots (Content child deactivated) so the collection reads as a silhouette of what remains (ChocographUI.cs:290-316, 428); the sheet carries an up/down ScrollButton rail (child 0) and a caption header block (child 2: top-border/border/body sprites + its own caption UIPanel with name/info labels) per the GOScrollablePanel anatomy (GOScrollablePanel.cs:15-17, 28-66); (3) a browse-time picture pane (HintContentPanel) holding the map artwork sprite (HintMap, sprite "chocograph_map_NN" from a dedicated scene-baked ChocographAtlas), the flavor/detail text (HintText), and a 5-slot required-ability icon strip (HintAbilityRequiredPanel) — shown only while the cursor rests on a discovered row (ChocographUI.cs:189-206, 335-346); (4) an equipped pane (SelectedContentPanel) repeating map picture + box icon + name for the currently equipped chocograph, active only when one is equipped (ChocographUI.cs:392-399); (5) a chocobo-ability progression strip of 5 icon sprites (ChocoboAbilityInfoPanel) plus two counters — maps in inventory and dig-sites found (ChocographUI.cs:264-274); (6) a two-button submenu row, Select/Cancel, where Cancel greys out via label color + button animation when nothing is equipped (ChocographUI.cs:369-381); (7) a PC-only help caption (HelpDespLabelGameObject, ChocographUI.cs:32) and the HonoFading screen-fade sprite. Left/right placement of list vs picture pane is baked in the scene and not recoverable from source (all right-pane geometry is inspector-serialized; only the list gets runtime numbers). Interaction is two-level: SubMenu group first, Confirm on Select drops into the Item list group; picking a discovered+reachable row equips it and writes hintmap_id into save state, which the WorldHUD then renders as a docked map picture next to the minimap (WorldHUD.cs:847-866, panel nudged +158,-708 at WorldHUD.cs:1244).

screens.depth_stack: Baked panel depths are inspector-serialized and not recoverable from source. Runtime-written depth facts: pointer depth for the Item list group = 4 (ChocographUI.cs:15) — the shared menu convention (ItemUI/AbilityUI also 4); the SubMenu group sets none, so its pointer falls back to PointerManager default depth 5 (ButtonGroupState.cs:649); the help bubble renders at pointer depth - 1 = 3 (ButtonGroupState.cs:542). Structural sorting: the list SubPanel is a clipping UIPanel (GOSubPanel.cs:24, baseClipRegion write at :50) while the caption block owns a separate CaptionPanel UIPanel (GOScrollablePanel.cs:47), so header text sorts independently above the clipped rows. HintContentPanel / SelectedContentPanel layering is handled by SetActive toggling, never by depth writes (ChocographUI.cs:132, 196-201, 278-279, 395).
screens.pointer: Two button groups: "Chocograph.SubMenu" and "Chocograph.Item" (ChocographUI.cs:429-430). Item group config (all in the Show after-fade delegate, ChocographUI.cs:13-21): pointer depth 4 (:15); finger offset (30, 0) (:16); limit rect derived from the ChocographListPanel root UIWidget + ItemHeight — left/right = widget x -/+ width/2, bottom = y - h/2 - 14 + itemHeight/2, top = y + h/2 - 20 - itemHeight/2 (ButtonGroupState.cs:206-217); the ScrollButton is bound to the group so bumpers page it (ChocographUI.cs:18; UIScene.cs:168-186). SubMenu group: no pointer depth/offset/rect set — engine defaults (pointer depth 5, ButtonGroupState.cs:649). While the list is active the SubMenu is put in secondary + hold-active state (ChocographUI.cs:120-121). Cursor memory: removed for SubMenu on entry (:19) and for Item on Hide (:83-86); start-select re-seeded to the equipped row or row 0 on Show (:33-45).
screens.transitions: Enter: only via the field-script menu op — FF9Menu_Command case 5 → OpenChocoGraph (EventService.cs:6-27, 59-70): closes all dialogs, drops the field icon + bubble UI, Hide()s the current scene (that scene's own fade-in plays), then ChangeUIState(Chocograph). ChocographUI.Show first calls SceneDirector.FadeEventSetColor(FadeMode.Sub, Color.black) to neutralize any event-engine shader tint (ChocographUI.cs:24; SceneDirector.cs:573-579), then UIScene.Show runs the window-color sweep and the HonoFading fade-out over Configuration.Interface.FadeDuration (default 40) (UIScene.cs:45-57; InterfaceSection.cs:76); the pointer/group config runs in the after-fade delegate (ChocographUI.cs:13-21). Leave: Cancel at SubMenu level → SFX 101 → Hide → fade-in → MainMenuUI.UIControlPanel?.ExitMenu() + ChangeUIState(HUDState) (ChocographUI.cs:70-81, 170-178). No tween/position animation on any pane — this screen is pure fade + SetActive. SFX vocabulary: 103 = descend into the list (ChocographUI.cs:117); 107 = equip a map AND un-equip via Cancel (:127, :155); 102 = refused (blank row, unreachable, or Cancel with nothing equipped) (:136, :147, :152); 101 = back out (:176, :181); OnSecondaryGroupClick mutes SFX while re-routing a cross-group click (:213-215). Side effect on leave-state: equipping writes FF9StateSystem.Common.FF9.hintmap_id = 1+index (:157), which WorldHUD.DisplayChocographLocation renders as a docked "chocograph_map_NN" picture panel beside the minimap (WorldHUD.cs:847-866; panel offset +158,-708 written at WorldHUD.cs:1244).
screens.window_color: One scene-wide sweep only: UIScene.Show → DisplayWindowBackground() on the whole scene root (UIScene.cs:47-48), re-atlasing every UISprite tagged "Window Color" to FF9UIDataTool.WindowAtlas (grey/blue per player setting), skipping sprites already on GeneralAtlas/IconAtlas (UIScene.cs:261-273). ChocographUI neither overrides it nor adds per-row sweeps. The map pictures and box/ability icons are untouched by the sweep — they live on the dedicated scene-baked ChocographAtlas (FF9UIDataTool.cs:345 reads it off the HintMap sprite).
screens.widescreen_pass: UpdateUserInterface (ChocographUI.cs:49-68), called from Show (:26), gated on Configuration.Interface.IsEnabled (:51). It re-dimensions ONLY the list; every other pane keeps its bake. Constants: originalLineCount=5, buttonOriginalHeight=86f, panelOriginalWidth=658f, panelOriginalHeight=5*86=430 (:53-56). linePerPage = MenuChocographRowCount (default 7 — InterfaceSection.cs:71, Memoria.ini:330; PC stock bake is 5, PSX was 7 per the comment), lineHeight = round(430/linePerPage) = 61 at 7 rows, scaleFactor = 61/86 ≈ 0.709 (:57-59). ChangeDims(1, 7, 658f, 61) (:60) → SnapDragScrollView.ItemHeight=61, VisibleItem=7, table columns=1, panel baseClipRegion w/h = 658 x 427 with anchor cleared (GOSubPanel.cs:42-50); static path: each button SetDimensions(658, 61) then an end-of-frame reposition with pivotOffset (0, .5) and SetRawRect(posX, -posY, 658, 61) (GOSubPanel.cs:61-67, 71-87). Per-button re-anchor (ChocographUI.cs:61-67): IconSprite → target row transform, relBottom/relTop .5 with bottom -36*scale / top +36*scale, relLeft/relRight .064 with right +72*scale (≈51x51 px icon at 7 rows); NameLabel → relBottom .081 / relTop .919, relLeft .064 with left +90*scale, relRight 1; fontSize = round(36*scale) = 26; effectDistance = (3,3). This is the truest runtime record: the stock list cell is a 658x86 row with a 72px icon inset at 6.4% and a size-36 label starting 90px further in, all scaled proportionally when the row count changes.
idioms: STATIC baked list, no populator: 24 row GOs live in the scene and are enumerated from the table transform in Awake (ChocographUI.cs:406-410); GOSubPanel.cs:74 comment confirms Chocograph is the game's only GOSubPanel without a RecycleListPopulator — its reposition path is written just for this screen.

Silhouette grammar for undiscovered entries: the row button stays in the group but its child-0 'Content' is SetActive(false), leaving a blank slot; confirm on it = buzzer 102 with Help disabled (ChocographUI.cs:145-149, 292, 309-316).

State encoded as sprite-name variants: box open/closed x reachable/'_null' grey (ChocographUI.cs:296-299, 318-333) and ability icons swapping to 'chocograph_icon_unknown_null' for unearned tiers (:341-345, 363) — no tinting, purely alternate atlas sprites, plus label color White/Gray (:301).

Two-group hold pattern: dropping into the list sets the parent SubMenu group Secondary + HoldActiveState so its highlight persists (ChocographUI.cs:118-121); a mouse click on the held group is re-routed by muting SFX, faking Cancel, then Confirm (:208-218).

Pointer-per-group config re-applied in the Show after-fade delegate every entry: depth, offset, limit rect from the panel widget + itemHeight with the -14/-20 fudge, scroll-button binding (ChocographUI.cs:13-21; ButtonGroupState.cs:206-217).

Awake anchor micro-surgery on baked labels: rightAnchor.Set(1f,-40) on two deep-path labels + full-width stretch on the SubMenu labels + fixedAlignment (ChocographUI.cs:419-425) — imperative one-off fixes layered over the bake.
Disabled-button = label color + animation toggle, not removal: SetCancelButton greys the label and SetButtonAnimation(false) (ChocographUI.cs:369-381).

Cross-screen persistence through save state, not UI state: static CurrentSelectedChocograph mirrored from FF9StateSystem.Common.FF9.hintmap_id (ChocographUI.cs:225-236), re-seeded on every Show (:33-45) and consumed by WorldHUD's docked map picture (WorldHUD.cs:847-866).

Dedicated content atlas baked into the scene: FF9UIDataTool.ChocographAtlas is defined as 'whatever atlas the HintMap sprite carries' (FF9UIDataTool.cs:345) — the picture pane's art source is scene data, code only writes sprite names.
OnLocalize live-language refresh re-writes visible list names, help keys, hint text and the equipped label in place (ChocographUI.cs:88-106).

screens.depth_stack: No PANEL depth is written anywhere in CardUI — the whole z-order is baked in the prefab. Back-to-front by structure: menu background cloth (root child 6, CardUI.cs:488) -> the three content panes (PlayerInfoPanel / CardSelectionListPanel / CardInfoPanel, baked depths) -> the discard dialog, which is its own GOPanel with a nested TextPanel UIPanel (CardUI.cs:627-635) so it sorts as a separate panel above the sheet; Memoria sets its Panel.clipping=None when the Auto button makes it taller than the baked clip (CardUI.cs:649) -> the HonoFading screen-fade sprite on top (CardUI.cs:452; UIScene.cs:99-100). The only explicit depth number on this screen is the POINTER depth: 2 for the grid group (CardUI.cs:20) versus the engine default 5 (ButtonGroupState.cs:649) — the finger is deliberately pushed DOWN the stack so it tucks under/behind adjacent card cells rather than floating over the whole grid.
screens.pointer: Two button groups: 'Card.Card' (the grid + mobile Delete button, CardUI.cs:497) and 'Card.Choice' (discard choices, CardUI.cs:498). Configured in Show (CardUI.cs:20-22): SetPointerDepthToGroup(2, Card.Card) — grid pointer at depth 2, dialog group left at the default depth 5 (ButtonGroupState.cs:649); SetPointerOffsetToGroup((60,10), Card.Choice) — dialog finger pushed 60 right / 10 up, x mirrored under RTL (ButtonGroupState.cs:652-661); grid group gets the default offset (0,0). NO pointer limit rect is set for either group -> both fall back to the full-screen rect UIManager.UIScreenCoOrdinate (ButtonGroupState.cs:648; UIManager.cs:49) — consistent with a non-scrolling list needing no containment. No SetPointerNumberToGroup (single finger). Modal handoff: dialog open = RemoveCursorMemorize(Card.Choice) + ActiveGroup=Card.Choice + HoldActiveStateOnGroup(Card.Card) so the grid selection stays lit under the dialog (CardUI.cs:87-89); the grid's cursor memorize is cleared on scene exit (CardUI.cs:43, 57-60). During the L1/R1 stack shuffle the pointer is kept visible while input locks: ShowPointerWhenLoading=true + Loading=true (CardUI.cs:222-223, 246-247).
screens.transitions: ENTER: MainMenu 'Card' row sets the submenu clip shift (0, 9 + shiftFactor*490) and hides itself, then ChangeUIState(Card) (MainMenuUI.cs:182-191). CardUI.Show: SceneDirector.FadeEventSetColor(Sub, black) (CardUI.cs:26), base UIScene fade-out via HonoFading at Configuration.Interface.FadeDuration (UIScene.cs:52-57), then after-show: MainMenuScene.SubMenuPanel.SetActive(false) + pointer config + ActiveGroup=Card.Card (CardUI.cs:19-22). LEAVE (cancel): SFX 101, Hide -> NeedTweenAndHideSubMenu=false, CurrentSubMenu=Card, ChangeUIState(MainMenu) (CardUI.cs:183-190); Hide also restarts the main-menu submenu tween and clears cursor memorize when !fastSwitch (CardUI.cs:40-44) — and fastSwitch is never set true in stock CardUI (declared CardUI.cs:539, only ever assigned false at 184): Card does NOT participate in the L1/R1 fast-switch carousel the four character submenus share. IN-SCENE: discard dialog = HonoTweenClipping window-grow TweenIn/TweenOut, default AnimationTime 0.16s (HonoTweenClipping.cs:193), message text hidden during the clip and shown after (CardUI.cs:90-92); duplicate-stack shuffle on L1/R1 = HonoTweenPosition.TweenPingPong over up to 4 sub-card indexes (CardUI.cs:220-229, 244-253), component defaults duration 0.4s + resetAnchorDelay 0.2s, slide-in x=1543 / slide-out x=-1543 (HonoTweenPosition.cs:280-288). SFX ids: 103 = confirm/open-dialog/discard-executed (CardUI.cs:82, 147, 160); 102 = refuse-buzzer on an empty slot (CardUI.cs:99); 101 = cancel (CardUI.cs:134, 183, 196); 1047 = the L1/R1 stack-cycle flip (CardUI.cs:218, 242 — the same id the other screens use for page flips).
screens.window_color: One scene-wide sweep, not per-row: UIScene.Show calls this.DisplayWindowBackground() before the fade (UIScene.cs:48), which walks GetComponentsInChildren<UISprite>(true) — including inactive panes like the closed discard dialog — and re-atlases every sprite tagged 'Window Color' to FF9UIDataTool.WindowAtlas (grey/blue per setting), skipping General/Icon atlas sprites (UIScene.cs:261-273). screens.layout_summary: The Config screen is the game's one "control sheet" menu: a single dominant full-width, single-column list of control rows (ConfigList) over a full-screen background cloth, with no side panes. Each row is a full-width widget seating a left title label and a right-side control — either a two-choice toggle (two label buttons) or a min/max slider group. The list is a snap-scrolling panel (SnapDragScrollView) with an up/down arrow rail (ScrollButton at ConfigList child 0) and rows in ConfigList.GetChild(1).GetChild(0) (ConfigUI.cs:1531, 1611-1612). Below the list sits the Booster strip (BoosterPanel: MasterSkill/LvMax/GilMax cheat buttons, ConfigUI.cs:1618-1620); when Memoria disables cheats the strip is destroyed and the list grows 2 more visible rows, its bottom anchor dropping to -940 (ConfigUI.cs:1640-1646). Interactive region when boosters are present: the pointer limit rect written for the booster zone is x -745..745, y -370..321 — i.e. the sheet's column is 1490 UI-units wide, centered (ConfigUI.cs:946). Two modal layers ride on top: (1) the To-Title Warning dialog — a framed window (GOFrameBackground: Caption/Body/Border/Shadow) with two free-standing Yes/No labels, opened by a clip-grow tween (HonoTweenClipping) behind a full-screen hit catcher (ConfigUI.cs:703-713, 1614-1615, 1633-1634); (2) the controller-remap sub-screen — Keyboard/Joystick type buttons plus per-platform CustomController panels whose rows show new-vs-default key bindings; modality is done purely by button-group swap with HoldActiveStateOnGroup, the list remaining visible behind (ConfigUI.cs:238-250, 795-803). A PC-only help caption label exists but is force-hidden (ConfigUI.cs:630-634), and help bubbles are disabled for the whole screen (HelpEnabled=false, ConfigUI.cs:619,633; OnKeySelect returns false, ConfigUI.cs:670-673). The screen reads visually as: one tall sheet of uniform rows, arrows top/bottom of the rail, cheat strip at the bottom, everything on the menu cloth.

Row width: the interactive column spans x -745..745 => 1490 (ConfigUI.cs:946). CELL ANATOMY — every row is a GameObject with UIWidget + ButtonGroupState + ScrollItemKeyNavigation + UIKeyNavigation + a BoxCollider (the ROW is the button; controls inside are sub-targets). Toggle row: child 0 = title label (UILocalize key = enum name, ConfigUI.cs:1441), child 1 = choice A, child 2 = choice B, each choice's child 0 = UILabel (1583-1584, 1303-1304); selected choice label RGB 0.784 grey-white, unselected 0.392 grey (1306-1311). Slider row: child 0 = title label; child 1 = slider group (GOConfigSliderMinMax, ConfigUI.cs:1656-1673): .child 0 = Min label, .child 1 = UISlider object (UISprite track + child 0 bar + child 1 thumb, GOSlider.cs:17-22), .child 2 = Max label (fixedAlignment), .child 3 = Highlight UISprite, .child 4 = thin window background (GOThinBackground: sprite + child 0 border); the interactive ConfigChoice[0] = row.child(1).child(1) (1553). Volume rows re-purpose the Min-label slot as the numeric readout: row.GetChild(1).GetChild(0) rawText = round(value*20)*5 (1296); ATBMode row swaps its UILocalize key per value (1286-1292). Slider steps: volume = 21 steps (1489), ATBMode = 4 (1507), FieldMessage step divisor 6, BattleSpeed 2 (211-212); keyboard left/right moves 1/(numberOfSteps-1) (993-997). shared.topic: GO-wrapper vocabulary (Memoria/Scenes GO*.cs) — the named shape inventory of FF9's baked NGUI menu anatomy
shared.findings:
ALL wrappers live in C:/gd/FFIX/Memoria/Assembly-CSharp/Memoria/Scenes/. They are runtime typed views over the baked NGUI scene: each constructor's GetChild indices are assertions about the baked hierarchy, and GetExactComponent<T> (ExtensionMethodsGameObject.cs:11-26) throws with a component dump if the object does not carry exactly one component of the exact type — so a wrapper that constructs successfully is a verified schema of the baked shape. GetChild(i) is Transform.GetChild by index (Global/Game/GameObjectExtension.cs:6-14); FindChild is by name (GameObjectExtension.cs:21-24). Root class GOBase holds the GameObject, IsActive, an implicit GameObject conversion, and a compiled-constructor factory Create<T> (GOBase.cs:12-49).

== LEAF ATOMS (one NGUI component, no assumed children) ==
- GOWidget = UIWidget (GOWidget.cs:7-13). GOPanel = UIPanel (GOPanel.cs:7-13). GOSprite = UISprite (GOSprite.cs:7-13). GOLabel = UILabel with SetText writing Label.rawText and SetColor (GOLabel.cs:8-24). GOScrollBar = UIScrollBar (GOScrollBar.cs:5-14).
- GOLocalizableLabel = UILabel+UILocalize; sibling GOLocalizableSprite = UISprite+UILocalize in the same file (GOLocalizableLabel.cs:5-25).
- GOBlinkedLabel = UILabel+TweenAlpha — the blinking-text shape (GOBlinkedLabel.cs:5-14). GOAnimatedSprite = UISprite+UISpriteAnimation (GOAnimatedSprite.cs:6-15).

== BUTTON SHAPES ==
- GOWidgetButton = GOWidget + UIButton + BoxCollider + lazy UIEventListener (GOWidgetButton.cs:5-18). GOSpriteButton = UIButton + BoxCollider + UISprite (GOSpriteButton.cs:5-18).
- GOSimpleButton<T> = UIButton + BoxCollider + UIKeyNavigation + ButtonGroupState, with Content = Create<T>(obj) wrapping the SAME GameObject, not a child (GOSimpleButton.cs:15-25); runtime knob: Configuration.Control.WrapSomeMenus sets KeyNavigation.wrapUpDown (GOSimpleButton.cs:23-24). Used for dialog choice rows, e.g. ItemUI's Arrange dialog builds GOSimpleButton<GOLocalizableLabel> per choice (ItemUI.cs:1063,1070-1072).
- GONavigationButton — the classic selectable menu row: GOWidgetButton + UIKeyNavigation + ButtonGroupState; baked children 0=Name (GOLabel), 1=Highlight (GOSprite), 2=Background (GOThinBackground); the ctor forces Name overflow to ResizeFreely; SetLabelText/SetLabelColor helpers (GONavigationButton.cs:15-35). Battle command panel is six of these at children 0-5 (BattleHUD.UI.PanelCommand.cs:30-35).
- GOButtonPrefab — the LIST-ROW shape used by every scrolling list: components UIButton + BoxCollider + UIKeyNavigation + ButtonGroupState + ScrollItemKeyNavigation + UIDragScrollView + optional RecycleListItem (GOButtonPrefab.cs:27-34). Content anatomy is positional with one indirection: if child(0) itself has children, content = child(0); then optional IconSprite (+UISpriteAnimation) at the first slot, NameLabel next, NumberLabel next (GOButtonPrefab.cs:36-45); NameLabel.fixedAlignment forced true (GOButtonPrefab.cs:46-47).

== BACKGROUND / WINDOW SHAPES (the visual grammar) ==
- GOMenuBackground — the full-screen menu backdrop: root UISprite (baked sprite "menu_bg") + child(0) Shadow UISprite (baked "dialog_hilight") (GOMenuBackground.cs:14-15). Memoria's written-at-runtime layer: if an alternate name is passed AND the atlas contains it, the root re-sprites to the per-menu background and is sized to UIManager.UIContentSize (GOMenuBackground.cs:19-24); the Shadow is re-sprited "dialog_hilight"→"background_gradient" to uncouple the selection highlight from the menu gradient, also full-content-size (GOMenuBackground.cs:27-33). UIContentSize = (1080*aspect, 1080) widescreen else (1543, 1080) (Global/UI/UIManager.cs:653-665). Thirteen stock screens pass alternates, which also records each screen's baked child slot for the backdrop: main_menu_bg child4 (MainMenuUI.cs:819), item_bg child6 (ItemUI.cs:1030), ability_bg child7 (AbilityUI.cs:1526), equip_bg child6 (EquipUI.cs:1312), config_bg child8 (ConfigUI.cs:1652), card_bg child6 (CardUI.cs:488), chocograph_bg child7 (ChocographUI.cs:418), cloud_bg child9 (CloudUI.cs:854), party_setting_bg child5 (PartySettingUI.cs:506), save_load_bg child8 (SaveLoadUI.cs:716), shop_bg child7 (ShopUI.cs:1299), status_bg child10 (StatusUI.cs:456), battle_result_bg AllPanel child4 (BattleResultUI.cs:821).
- GOFrameBackground — the framed dialog window and the ONLY name-keyed wrapper: children found by name "Caption", "Body", "Border", "Shadow" with the comment "Not always in the same order" (GOFrameBackground.cs:15-19); ctor writes Caption.preventWrapping = true and overflow ClampContent (GOFrameBackground.cs:20-21). Users: ItemUI Arrange dialog child1 (ItemUI.cs:1073), ConfigUI warning dialog child1 (ConfigUI.cs:1634), AbilityUI detail child2 (AbilityUI.cs:1573), CardUI (CardUI.cs:612,635), BattleResultUI ability window (BattleResultUI.cs:947).
- GOThinBackground — the minimal window: own UIWidget + child(0) Border sprite, nothing else (GOThinBackground.cs:5-14). Standalone users: ConfigUI rows child4 (ConfigUI.cs:1670), TutorialUI child2 (TutorialUI.cs:438), battle HP/MP value widgets child3 and status-icon widgets child1 (BattleHUD.UI.ContainerStatus.cs:72,94); embedded as GONavigationButton child2 (GONavigationButton.cs:23).
- GOThinSpriteBackground — GOThinBackground + child(1) Body sprite, i.e. Border(0)+Body(1) (GOThinSpriteBackground.cs:5-14). Users: the battle HUD's Back/Toggle/Run buttons at child0 (BattleHUD.UI.ButtonBack.cs:28, BattleHUD.UI.ToggleButton.cs:31, BattleHUD.UI.ButtonRun.cs:28); derived caption variants append labels at children 2 (PanelCommand caption) and 2,3 (PanelTarget captions) per the dead-code record (Memoria/Scenes/BattleHUD/GOAllMenuPanel.cs:210-219,253-264).

== CONTAINERS / COMPOSITES ==
- GOArray<T> wraps EVERY child as T via the compiled-ctor factory (GOArray.cs:10-19). GOTable<T> = GOArray<T> + a UITable component on the parent (GOTable.cs:5-14).
- GOForegroundWidget: children 0=Highlight, 1=Foreground (GOForegroundWidget.cs:10-15).
- GOProgressBar — UISprite + UIProgressBar + child(0) GOForegroundWidget (GOProgressBar.cs:13-20); SetProgress smooths rising values by a per-frame step scaled BattleTPS/estimatedFps, and snaps instantly on decrease or fast-forward (GOProgressBar.cs:25-39).
- GOSlider — UISprite background + UISlider + BoxCollider + UIEventListener on the root, child0 SliderBar sprite, child1 SliderThumb sprite; notably uses plain GetComponent, not the exact-check (GOSlider.cs:14-23).

== THE SCROLLABLE-LIST COMPOUND (the game's one big shared list shape) ==
- GOScrollablePanel: baked children 0=ScrollButton, 1=SubPanel, 2=CaptionBackground (GOScrollablePanel.cs:15-17). Stock holders: AbilityUI x2 active/support (AbilityUI.cs:1524-1525), ChocographUI (ChocographUI.cs:413), EquipUI (EquipUI.cs:1294), ItemUI x2 item/keyitem (ItemUI.cs:1019-1020), ShopUI x3 buy-item/buy-weapon/sell (ShopUI.cs:1280-1282), BattleHUD ability+item at AllMenuPanel children 7,8 (BattleHUD.Unity.cs:86-87; BattleHUD.UI.AllMenuPanel.cs:36-37). (FolkloreUI.cs:407 is local DWIX code — excluded per brief.)
- GOScrollablePanel.CaptionBackground (the caption-topped window over the list): children 0=TopBorder, 1=Border, 2=Body, optional 3=Shadow (detected by child(3) carrying a UISprite), then CaptionPanel at 3 or 4 (GOScrollablePanel.cs:28-44). QUIRK/apparent bug: in the Shadow branch, Shadow = new GOSprite(obj.GetChild(2)) — the same child as Body — despite the branch keying on GetChild(3) (GOScrollablePanel.cs:34-36); the intended anatomy is clearly TopBorder/Border/Body/Shadow/Panel.
- GOScrollablePanel.CaptionPanel (a UIPanel of caption labels): child(0)=Name always; childCount 2 adds Info; childCount 4 adds Name2+Info2 — the two-column caption header (GOScrollablePanel.cs:54-65).
- GOScrollButton: components UIPanel + the stock ScrollButton MonoBehaviour; baked children 0=Up (GOSpriteButton), 1=Down (GOSpriteButton), 2=ScrollBar (GOScrollBar), 3=IgnoreAreaUp, 4=IgnoreAreaDown (both GOWidgetButton) (GOScrollButton.cs:19-26). ScrollButton behavior (Global/Scroll/ScrollButton.cs): scroll Offset defaults to SnapDragScrollView.ItemHeight (ScrollButton.cs:16-19), Speed default 48 (ScrollButton.cs:322), hold-to-repeat accelerates 1x→5x between 0.5s and 2.5s of hold with the repeat interval easing 0.2s→0.04s (ScrollButton.cs:281-310), end-of-list disables the arrow via UIButtonColor.State.Disabled + collider off (ScrollButton.cs:92-119), page-jump honors Configuration.Control.PSXScrollingMethod (ScrollButton.cs:199-252), scroll SFX id 103 (ScrollButton.cs:170).
- GOSubPanel — the clipped list viewport: UIPanel + UIScrollView + Rigidbody + SnapDragScrollView all on the same object; child(0) = GOTable<GOButtonPrefab>; optional RecycleListPopulator whose itemPrefab supplies the ButtonPrefab (GOSubPanel.cs:24-39). Two modes: recycling list (populator present — every stock list except one) vs static table (the Chocograph list is "currently the only GOSubPanel without list populator" per the comment at GOSubPanel.cs:74).
- GOSubPanel.ChangeDims(colCount,rowCount,colWidth,rowHeight) — THE resize API, written at runtime by every UpdateUserInterface pass: clamps counts ≥1 (GOSubPanel.cs:44-45); SnapDragScrollView.ItemHeight = rowHeight and VisibleItem = col*row (46-47); UITable.columns = colCount (48); Panel.SetAnchor(null) then baseClipRegion resized to (col*colWidth, row*rowHeight) keeping the clip center (49-50). Populator mode: cellHeight = rowHeight, prefab Widget.SetRawRect(0,0,colWidth,rowHeight), prefab ScrollKeyNavigation.ItemHeight = rowHeight, RefreshTableView if active (51-58). Static mode: per-entry SetDimensions then an end-of-frame reposition coroutine placing each cell at posX = padding.x + pivotOffset.x*width + col*(2*padding.x+width), posY mirrored, with a hardcoded pivotOffset (0, 0.5) hack for the chocograph list (GOSubPanel.cs:59-87).

- EquipUI: baked 5 rows x 1 col, row 90, panel 752 (EquipUI.cs:81-84); ChangeDims(1,rows,752,lineH) (EquipUI.cs:89).
- ChocographUI: baked 5 rows x 1 col, row 86, panel 658 (ChocographUI.cs:53-56); ChangeDims(1,...) (ChocographUI.cs:60) then per-entry restyle over Table.Entries since it is the static-mode list (ChocographUI.cs:61-67).

- Shared idioms at the call sites: the caption labels' two-column header fades to alpha 0 whenever runtime columns exceed the baked column count (ItemUI.cs:157-161; AbilityUI.cs:201-205; ShopUI.cs:100-104,151-155); the ScrollButton panel is dimmed to alpha 0.5 always (ItemUI.cs:133-134; AbilityUI.cs:160-161; ShopUI.cs:73-75) and to 0 when the list fits one page (AbilityUI.cs:207-208); border sprites are re-anchored with a ±3px outset on caption windows (BattleHUD.Public.cs:550,622).

== DEAD CODE THAT IS STILL A MAP ==
Memoria/Scenes/BattleHUD/GOAllMenuPanel.cs is entirely commented out (lines 1-349) but remains a legible record of the whole battle-HUD baked anatomy (AllMenuPanel children 0=Back 1=AllTarget 2=AutoAttack 3=Run 4=StatusContainer 5=CommandPanel 6=TargetPanel 7=AbilityPanel 8=ItemPanel 9=PartyPanel 10=AutoAttackHUD, GOAllMenuPanel.cs:25-35). The LIVE equivalents are partial classes at Global/battle/BattleHUD/BattleHUD.UI.*.cs using the same GO vocabulary and identical child indices (BattleHUD.UI.AllMenuPanel.cs:29-39), with children 7/8 typed as the shared GOScrollablePanel.

== WHAT IS BAKED VS WRITTEN ==
Baked (inferred from ctor bindings): every child index and component listed above; the sprite names "menu_bg" and "dialog_hilight" (they are the values GOMenuBackground tests against, GOMenuBackground.cs:19,28). Written at runtime: all ChangeDims geometry, SetRawRect/SetAnchor/SetDimensions calls, font sizes, alphas, the alternate background re-sprites, GOFrameBackground's caption overflow policy, GONavigationButton's ResizeFreely, GOButtonPrefab's fixedAlignment, and GOSimpleButton's wrapUpDown.
idioms: A GO wrapper constructor is a schema assertion: GetChild indices name the baked anatomy and GetExactComponent throws unless exactly one component of the exact type exists (ExtensionMethodsGameObject.cs:11-26) — construction succeeding proves the shape.

The scrollable-list trinity: every scrolling menu list in the game is child 0=ScrollButton, 1=SubPanel, 2=CaptionBackground under one GOScrollablePanel (GOScrollablePanel.cs:15-17) — Item, KeyItem, Ability x2, Equip, Chocograph, Shop x3, Battle ability+item.

The window-weight ladder: full-screen backdrop (menu_bg + dialog_hilight shadow) > framed dialog (Caption/Body/Border/Shadow, name-keyed) > caption window (TopBorder/Border/Body + label panel) > thin sprite window (Border+Body) > thin window (Border only).

== 1. SCENE TRANSITION GRAMMAR ==

Every menu screen derives from UIScene (Global/UI/UIScene.cs:8). The transition is a THREE-LAYER composition: (a) a full-screen alpha fade, (b) an optional panel position-tween, (c) an optional clip-region grow/shrink — each screen picks which layers it spends.

(a) The fade. UIScene.Show (UIScene.cs:45-65) activates the GameObject, runs DisplayWindowBackground (line 48), then if `fading != null && isNeedFade` sets `fading.fadeOutDuration = Configuration.Interface.FadeDuration` (divided by FastForwardFactor when fast-forwarding) and calls `fading.FadeOut(AfterSceneShown)` with `Loading = true` (lines 52-57). Hide is the mirror: `fading.FadeIn(AfterSceneHidden)` (UIScene.cs:74-92). HonoFading (Global/Hono/HonoFading.cs) is a black foreground UISprite driven by a TweenAlpha: FadeOut = from-black reveal (fadeOutFrom=1 → fadeOutTo=0, HonoFading.cs:66-70, 146-150), FadeIn = to-black cover (fadeInFrom=0 → fadeInTo=1, lines 60-64, 136-140). Baked default duration is 0.4 s both ways (HonoFading.cs:140,150) but every Show/Hide overwrites it with Configuration.Interface.FadeDuration = 40 ms Memoria default, 300 ms original game, clamped 0-5 s (Memoria/Configuration/Structure/InterfaceSection.cs:76; Memoria/Configuration/Memoria.ini:302; Memoria/Configuration/Access/Interface.cs:128-131). Anti-flash guard: durations ≤ 0.05 s skip the black entirely (HonoFading.cs:62-69). The fade sprite is widescreen-rescaled per fade (HonoFading.cs:36-41). Completion is timer-based, not tween-callback-based: WaitForSeconds(duration+delay) (HonoFading.cs:102-111).

Lifecycle bookkeeping: AfterShow resets Loading=false, isNeedToHide=true, isNeedFade=true (UIScene.cs:67-72). AfterHide deactivates the GameObject only if isNeedToHide, and force-zeros the fade sprite's alpha (UIScene.cs:94-101). `NextSceneIsModal = true` sets isNeedFade=false AND isNeedToHide=false (UIScene.cs:16-24) — the modal-overlay idiom: the next screen appears instantly and the current one stays alive underneath. The Loading flag is the input gate: every OnKey* virtual returns false while isLoading (e.g. UIScene.cs:108-120), and Update syncs it to the chrome — Loading=true hides ALL pointers and disables the active button group; Loading=false restores both (UIScene.cs:280-298, via PointerManager.SetAllPointerVisibility and ButtonGroupState.SetActiveGroupEnable).

(b) The panel tween — HonoTweenPosition (Global/Hono/Tween/HonoTweenPosition.cs). An array of "dialog" GameObjects each gets a TweenPosition; TweenIn slides each from `animatedInStartPosition` (default (1543, 0) — one full pillarboxed screen-width to the right, line 280; out-end default (−1543,0), line 282) to its baked rest position captured at Awake (`stopedPositionList`, line 54). Shared `duration` default 0.4 s (line 288) plus a per-panel `delayList` stagger (lines 131-137) — the staggered-slide-in look. During flight the widget's anchors are detached and restored after `resetAnchorDelay` = 0.2 s (lines 209-215, 231-246). ABSOLUTE mode tweens relative to rest position instead (lines 116-122); `snapYPosition` slides x-only (123-130); `deactiveAfterTweenOut` (default true, line 304) hides panels after the out-tween. == 3. THE POINTER SYSTEM ==

PointerManager (Global/PointerManager.cs) is a singleton pool. `pointerPool`/`activePointerList`/`attachList` (Dictionary<GameObject,UIPointer>) at lines 30-32, 179-181. AttachPointerToGameObject (35-63) reuses an attached pointer (refreshing its offset/limit rect from the manager's current values, 44-49) or pulls one from the pool, names it "<target> Pointer" (53), and attaches. Pointers live under per-DEPTH pooled panels: PointerPanelManager.GetPanel(depth) creates one UIPanel per distinct depth value and caches it forever (lines 187-208) — the pointer's draw order is a PANEL depth. Default pointerDepth = 5 (line 185; GetPointerFromPool default arg, line 134). Static PointerManager.PointerSize = (114, 62) (line 177); UIPointer.PointerSize is re-captured from the actual widget at attach (Global/UI/UIPointer.cs:35).

Per-GROUP configuration lives in ButtonGroupState statics keyed by group name (Global/Button/ButtonGroupState.cs:666-670): SetPointerOffsetToGroup (196), SetPointerLimitRectToGroup Vector4 form (201) and the list-window helper form (206-218) which derives the rect from a widget: left = x−w/2, bottom = y−h/2−14+itemHeight/2, right = x+w/2, top = y+h/2−20−itemHeight/2 — the −14/−20 insets are the stock list-rail margins. SetPointerDepthToGroup (220), SetPointerNumberToGroup (225), SetOutsideLimitRectBehavior (230). On group activation UpdatePointerPropertyForGroup pushes these into the manager with defaults: offset (0,0) (x mirrored under RTL, 652-661), limit rect = UIManager.UIScreenCoOrdinate = full screen (±w/2, ±h/2) (648; Global/UI/UIManager.cs:49), depth = 5 (649).

LimitRectBehavior (PointerManager.cs:211-216): Limit clamps the position into the rect (UIPointer.cs:80-84); Hide blanks the sprite when > 2 px outside (61-79); None ignores. Default on every hover-attach is Limit unless the group registered otherwise (ButtonGroupState.cs:441-444). Blink = enabling the pointer's baked TweenAlpha (UIPointer.cs:112-122, bound in Awake at 206) — used for held-state and multi-target cursors (ButtonGroupState.HoldActiveStateOnGroup 246-258, SetAllTarget 355-385, SetMultipleTarget 387-420, which also disable the group's colliders while all-target is on). The battle target-number badge is child 0, sprite "hand_battle_{n}" (UIPointer.cs:147-161). Groups can opt out of the cursor entirely via ButtonGroupState.DisablePointerCursor (664, checked at 438).

== 5. THE HELP / TUTORIAL BUBBLE SHAPE ==

HelpDialog (Global/HelpDialog.cs) is a singleton bubble whose anatomy is baked as five children bound in Awake (256-267): child 0 = body widget, child 1 = border widget, child 2 = caption widget, child 3 = phrase UILabel (default text color FF9TextTool.DarkBlue, line 266; fontSize 42, line 108), child 4 = tail UISprite. Runtime shape math (InitializeDialog, 104-176): the body is sized to the measured text (FF9Help_ComputeWindow, 178-223: width = Parser.MaxWidth + FF9HELP_X_SPACE, height = RawHeight + FF9HELP_Y_SPACE, clamped to a clip rect); the border is ALWAYS body + 36 px in each dimension (169-170) — the frame overhang constant; the caption pins to the top-left corner at 22 px inset, half-out of the body (171); text padding X=30 / Y=58 inside body padding X=18 / Y=62 (297-300); the whole thing is one UIPanel whose baseClipRegion and depth are set per show (165-166) — the depth comes from ButtonGroupState.ShowHelpDialog as (group pointer depth − 1), default 4 (ButtonGroupState.cs:542), i.e. the bubble always draws one panel below its pointer. Tail placement is quadrant-chosen by free space around the anchor (190-222, gap constants scaled by ResourceMultipliers at 269-277) and rendered with the shared "dialog_pointer_*" caps (225-254); Tail=false suppresses it (183-188). Battle repurposes the same bubble as the fixed command-description panel with hardcoded rects — target group (1282, 898, 478×272) vs command group (1116.5, 898, 808×264), the official-patch resize noted in comments (127-157). Anchoring: ShowHelpDialog computes the position from the active button's widget worldCenter minus half its width (RTL: plus width + 3/4 pointer width) (ButtonGroupState.cs:534-543). The toggle is the Select key → ButtonGroupState.ToggleHelp, SFX 682 on / 101 off, disabled on WorldHUD and the quit prompt (UIScene.cs:146-152; ButtonGroupState.cs:477-496); help display first plays the moogle: the pointer's child-1 sprite runs "help_mog_hand_1" through a baked TweenScale, then swaps to "help_mog_hand_2" and only then shows the dialog (UIPointer.cs:173-191). Hiding all pointers hides the dialog; re-showing re-opens it if the active button has Help.Enable (PointerManager.cs:108-125). Per-button help content is the serialized HelpDetail {Enable, TextKey, Text, Tail} on ButtonGroupState (ButtonGroupState.cs:689-696).

The FIELD bubble (Global/Bubble/BubbleUI.cs) is a separate system: the contextual action balloon over the player, toggled by UIScene only for FieldHUD/WorldHUD (UIScene.cs:62-64, 89-91), with primary/secondary button sprites "button_minigame", "button_bubble_question_idle", "button_card_idle", "button_beach_idle" (BubbleUI.cs:250-272).
